channel.title: PauloGerm (EN)
channel.description: Development notebook, projects and studies — English edition.

item.title: Local Player: transcode fallback and Whisper in a P0-P3 queue
item.description: Compatible files play directly via Range. Incompatible ones become fragmented MP4 with 416 seek. Subtitles are an add-on: never await before video.play().

item.title: Local Player: atomic progress that travels with the drive
item.description: How writeFileAtomic + serial queue + .bak + .corrupt-<ts> eliminated position loss even when killing the server mid-save.

item.title: Local Player: vibecoding with invariants and zero build step
item.description: How a local/offline player in Express + vanilla JS organizes thousands of lessons with no bundler: AGENTS.md as contract, physical structure as source of truth, and scan with on-disk cache.

item.title: Java Fundamentals: why Java succeeded
item.description: Explanation of the technical reasons that helped Java grow, focusing on portability, the JVM, bytecode, and .class files.

item.title: Java Fundamentals: what is a programming language
item.description: Introductory explanation of programming languages, Java, bytecode, the JVM, and common areas where the language is used.

item.title: Java Fundamentals: object-oriented principles
item.description: Practical explanation of the main OOP concepts, such as abstraction, encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, association, composition, and modularization.

item.title: Java Fundamentals: portability
item.description: Introductory explanation of portability in Java, the JVM, bytecode, and execution across different environments.

item.title: Java Fundamentals: the Java language
item.description: Overview of the Java language, its relationship with object orientation, the internet, bytecode, and the Java Virtual Machine.

item.title: Java Fundamentals: object orientation
item.description: Introduction to the object-oriented paradigm and the idea of representing problems through entities, objects, classes, and interactions.

item.title: ParkFlow: From Requirements Gathering to an AI-Assisted MVP
item.description: How we turned a real parking problem into an MVP with TypeScript, Supabase, license-plate-driven UX, and AI-assisted development.
